sentences.text: This animal possessed a boxy snout that ended in a flat, blunt front surface called the deltoid facet.
The preserved front base of the crest features a flat top margin, contrasting with the grooved surface seen in related species.
A small blunt protrusion at the crest base is unique to this group among anhanguerids.
The only known specimen was discovered in 2014 by Will Thurbin at Sudmour Point on the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, England.
The specimen was donated to the Dinosaur Isle museum and assigned the catalog number IWCMS 2014.82.
Tylodorhynchus is classified as a coloborhynchine anhanguerid and was established as a new genus for the species formerly known as Uktenadactylus rodriguesae.
The genus Tylodorhynchus was described by Pêgas and Holgado in 2026.
The species was reassigned to the new genus Tylodorhynchus because it differed from Uktenadactylus wadleighi, which was found to be more closely related to Nicorhynchus.
Tylodorhynchus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian stage.
Researchers suggest that the bulbous projection on Uktenadactylus wadleighi may be a pathology rather than a typical anatomical feature.
Initial assessments suggested that slight differences from Coloborhynchus clavirostris were not sufficient to warrant a distinct species status.
